title: [PDF] Supervisory Stress Test Documentation Credit Risk Models

source.name: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

summary: The Federal Reserve published updated documentation in January 2026 (original October 2025) for the credit risk models used in the 2026 Supervisory Stress Test (DFAST). The document details seven categories of credit risk models: Corporate, Commercial Real Estate, First Lien Mortgage, Home Equity, Credit Card, Auto, and Other Retail.
key_points: The document covers credit risk models for: Corporate, Commercial Real Estate (CRE), First Lien Mortgage, Home Equity, Credit Card, Auto, and Other Retail portfolios
January 2026 revisions added transparency on model coefficients and made technical corrections
Key model components include Probability of Default (PD), Loss Given Default (LGD), and related estimation methodologies
Each model section includes statement of purpose, model overview, key assumptions, and alternatives considered
why_it_matters: This technical documentation establishes the methodology the Fed uses to stress test bank balance sheets under adverse economic scenarios. While it affects bank capital planning and capital return capacity, it is not directly relevant to trading market structure or macro catalysts.
